recipes.name: Chef John’s Stuffed Summer Squash
ingredients_raw: 1 tablespoon dry bread crumbs, or more as needed

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil and lightly coat it with 1 teaspoon olive oil.

Heat 1 teaspoon olive oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat. Stir in sausage and red bell pepper. Cook, stirring to break up sausage into small pieces, until sausage is browned and bell pepper is soft and sweet, 7 to 8 minutes. Drain off any fat.
Stir goat cheese and sausage mixture in a bowl until well combined. Set aside.

Hollow out a 3/4-inch deep well in the center of each squash half. Place each piece on the prepared baking sheet, cut-side up. Season with salt and black pepper; fill each with 1 to 2 tablespoons cheese and sausage mixture. Top each squash with breadcrumbs and lightly drizzle with remaining 2 teaspoons olive oil.
Bake in the preheated oven until filling is golden and squash is tender, about 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Chef John’s Stuffed Summer Squash
raw_recipe.description: Summer squash paired with merguez sausage and goat cheese is the perfect recipe for a summer evening.

review.reviewBody:
It's CSA time and I was looking for something interesting to do with too much summer squash. This was delicious! I couldn't find the spicy lamb sausage, so I improvised: I used ground lamb and spiced it with minced onion and garlic, cumin, paprika, and cayenne as well as salt and black pepper. This seemed easier than removing the casing from an already prepared sausage anyway. I considered skipping the cheese to cut down on the richness, but decided to use feta instead of the goat cheese. It really added an interesting dimension, so I am glad I didn't leave it out. Because I didn't have the small round squash pictured, I used a larger elongated "mediterranean" squash, and it took longer to bake. More like 40 minutes. Both my husband and I gave it 5 stars. I will definitely use this recipe again.

Also, I felt badly about tossing the scooped out squash so I sauteed some onion and garlic along with the chopped up squash, added a half a seeded fresh tomato and stir fried the mixture with some cooked brown rice. It made the perfect side dish to accompany this meal.
Delicious and couldn't be easier. I used hot pork sausage, the kind that comes in the thick tubes, and garlic and herb bread crumbs. The red peppers add the most delightful kick!

I used zucchini and Italian sausage..... Fantastic! I also followed another reviewers recommendation and sautéed the scooped-out zucchini along with onion, garlic, green tomato, and brown rice....WOW! Everyone was eating it up as fast as they could! I can't wait to make this again!

If you're using yellow summer squash like in the picture, you'll need to make the following adjustments. I cooked three medium yellow squash, and I needed twice the amount of filling the original recipe calls for. Also, the squash needed to bake for about an hour. I put foil over it for second half of the baking time so the filling wouldn't burn. 

Like other reviewers, I used hot italian sausage. I also brushed olive oil over the squash and seasoned liberally with salt and pepper before adding the filling. Then I put a few pats of butter over the top of the bread crumbs.

It came out very tasty!

I also had a hard time finding the lamb sausage (San Antonio is dominated by one grocery chain and few finer food stores, sadly) so I used spicy Italian sausage with no other modifications. Amazing results! The video on this was very helpful, and I didn't expect goat cheese to pair so well with squash flavors/textures. As soon as I can get my hands on some merguez, I will definitely re-review.

I discovered this recipe a couple months ago and have made it about half a dozen times - I love it! Merguez is a little spicy for me, so I always use Italian sausage but otherwise make it as written. I've used the little round sausages in the video, but I've also used zucchini, yellow (crookneck) squash, and yesterday I used acorn squash (bonus: toasted squash seeds!). They're all delicious! Last week I made the filling using an entire package of Italian sausage, increasing the other ingredients accordingly. Then I divided it into fourths and froze them. Now I can just buy a squash and fill it very quickly! I plan to try delicata next. Thanks, Chef John!

I could not find merguez and didn't have time to make my own so I used hot italian sausage instead and this turned out incredible. I used zucchini from the garden because, well zucchini plants are ridiculously prodigious. I used 3 ounces of goat cheese because 2 was not enough and used panko on the top.

These are sooo good! Couldn't find lamb sausage so used Italian (I bet chorizo would be awesome too). And used regular small long zuchinni. Since its too hot to be using the oven I cooked them on our charcoal grill...and Wow! Gave them a great smoky taste with slight char on the bottom. Will make these over and over, thank you Chef John, love your recipes!

This turned out FREAKING AMAZING. 
The only adjustments I made was I didn't have the lamb sausage so I found a pound of ground lamb and added onion and garlic powder a little bit of cumin, Cayenne, smoked chipotle powder, smoked paprika salt and pepper to the lamb before I cooked it up.
Ratio wise, I used 2 small acorn squash and I didn't really scrape out much of the insides... Any insides that did get scraped out got thrown in the pan with the sausage and bell pepper... I also used 4 oz of garlic and herb goat cheese.

This was so good and quick to make. I had to tweak the recipe a little to use what I had available in my kitchen. I used 4 medium size Yellow squashes and for that I doubled the filling. I used Feta for goat cheese. Also, I couldn't help adding some chopped onions and garlic in, with the pepper. The grapefruit spoon did a great job scraping some of the seeds and flesh of the squash halves. I stuffed the squash halves in the morning, put them on a cookie sheet and covered and put in the fridge. I took them out an hour before dinner and let them come to room temperature for 30 minutes then baked and served.

I could have brought the Merguez sausage online but found the recipe online so started from fresh - lamb mince and spices. In the UK the supermarkets (I go to) only do butternut squashes so that's what I used. I mircowaved the squashes for five mins to make them cutable and then put them in the oven for half hour so I could scope them out. I lost the first one for being too vigorous in my scrapping but the other three were fine. I used 500g lamb mince and 70g goats cheese but I suspect I probably needed more cheese for that amount of lamb. Very tasty for a treat. Made fried rice and squash to go with it.

A keeper recipe that can be altered depending on available ingredients. And goes down real easy! I had a fat Italian Squash around 3" diameter. I cut horizontally around 1-1/2" wide rounds, removed seeds, covered inside and out with olive oil to hold salt and pepper, shaken or ground. No sausage available and wanted lower fat, so I used 4 Meatless Meatballs. Made 3 cuts vertically and one horizontal making 6 pieces each ball. I mixed 1 T Soy Sauce, 2 T water or wine, 1 teaspoon fennel and 1/2 teaspoon Sofrito in a bowl, then poured over the cut meatballs, turning until mostly absorbed. These I sauteed until hot and no excess liquid was left in the pan. This then substituted for the sausage. Then I followed the recipe. Finally, top the breadcrumbs with grated Parmigiana or Pecorino/Romano. The result after baking was moist, flavorful, and healthy. Served with rice of choice, which for me is 50/50 brown and red cargo rice cooked with 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder and 1/4 teaspoon turmeric in 4 cups rice.
I had these cute perfectly round squash in my garden. Used Italian sausage, added garlic and crispy onions to top. Husband ate two!!! Yummy!

Delicious. I totally revamped it but as a base it was a great recipe. I used Chimichuri Chicken sausage and a blend of tiny sweet red, orange and yellow peppers and a jalapeño for kick. Yellow onion, shallot and garlic. Instead of bread crumbs, Parmesan. Yummy!!
it was OK,,,,I used Italian sausage which I thought was a bit salty.....the overall recipe was easy to prepare...

This looks like zucchini was used even though I’ve never seen zucchini shaped like that. I’m gonna use yellow squash. They are really small and use regular ground pan sausage. I know it will turn out amazing. I’m gonna salt and pepper liberally like some have done too.

This was a great low carb treat. I used my giant overgrown zucchini from my garden, stuffed with ground beef and Italian sausage, mixed spaghetti sauce into meat mixture and then topped it with shredded cheese. Was a little bland so I topped it with a nice portion of Old Bay to add flavor and spices.
Made it. Loved it. Easy and tasty.b
The most surprising feature of this recipe was the fact that I did not feel hungry a short while after eating it. We ate this as an entree and were satisfied.
Great recipe!
